gloss_distractors: a tool that scans for bugs
a monitor that watches server speed
senses.definition: A background process that finds and removes stuck, expired, or orphaned tasks.
senses.caution: Say what it removes, such as sessions, jobs, or dead child processes. The word alone does not tell you whether it only reports or also kills.
senses.example: A reaper runs every minute and kills any job that has not sent a heartbeat for ten minutes.

cues.text: Jobs stay in the running state after their worker crashed, so you add a background process that finds them and marks them failed. What do you call that process, using the harvest-themed name?
In a code review you see a loop that wakes every minute and deletes expired sessions. A teammate asks what the component doing this cleanup is usually called.
A server fills up with orphaned child processes that nobody waits on, and you need the harvest-themed name for the component that gathers up the dead ones.

distractors: A tool that sends an alert when a server runs slowly.
A service that copies every change to a second database so that nothing is lost if the first fails.
A scheduler that decides when each job should start running during the day and in what order.
A script that checks code for style mistakes before it is merged.
A queue that holds messages until a worker is free to handle them.
